Exercise Q1 & 2

Answer the questions first. Check the answers and explanations only when ready.Jawab soalan dahulu. Semak jawapan dan penerangan apabila sudah bersedia.

Question 1

Which pair forms the central nervous system? [1]
Pasangan manakah membentuk sistem saraf pusat?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: B

[1] B: Brain and spinal cord

Jawapan yang betul: B — Otak dan saraf tunjang

The central nervous system consists of the brain and spinal cord; cranial and spinal nerves belong to the peripheral nervous system.

Question 2

A student hears a timer and then presses its stop button. Which route carries sensory impulses? [1]
Seorang murid mendengar pemasa lalu menekan butang henti. Laluan manakah membawa impuls deria?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: C

[1] C: Receptors in the ear to the brain

Jawapan yang betul: C — Reseptor dalam telinga ke otak

Sensory impulses carry detected information from receptors towards the central nervous system.

Question 3

Which action normally involves a conscious decision? [1]
Tindakan manakah biasanya melibatkan keputusan sedar?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: D

[1] D: Choosing to lift a bag from the floor

Jawapan yang betul: D — Memilih untuk mengangkat beg dari lantai

Choosing and lifting the bag is voluntary; the other examples normally occur without a conscious decision.

Question 4

A student sees a rolling ball and moves her leg to stop it. Which structure acts as an effector in this response? [1]
Seorang murid melihat bola bergolek lalu menggerakkan kakinya untuk menghentikannya. Struktur manakah bertindak sebagai efektor dalam gerak balas ini?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: A

[1] A: Leg muscles

Jawapan yang betul: A — Otot kaki

Muscles carry out the movement; receptors detect, nerves carry impulses and the brain coordinates the action.

Exercise Q5 & 6

Answer the questions first. Check the answers and explanations only when ready.Jawab soalan dahulu. Semak jawapan dan penerangan apabila sudah bersedia.

Question 5

Which statement correctly distinguishes the two main divisions of the nervous system? [1]
Pernyataan manakah membezakan dua bahagian utama sistem saraf dengan betul?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: D

[1] D: The peripheral system links body parts to the central system through cranial and spinal nerves.

Jawapan yang betul: D — Sistem periferi menghubungkan bahagian badan dengan sistem pusat melalui saraf kranium dan saraf spina.

Peripheral nerves connect body structures with the brain and spinal cord; they are not restricted to the limbs.

Question 6

After a student moves from a bright corridor into a dim room, which change normally allows more light into the eyes? [1]
Selepas seorang murid bergerak dari koridor terang ke bilik malap, perubahan manakah biasanya membenarkan lebih banyak cahaya memasuki mata?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: C

[1] C: The pupil becomes larger.

Jawapan yang betul: C — Pupil membesar.

Pupil enlargement increases the opening for light; lens-thickness changes concern focusing rather than controlling light entry.

Review Answer · Q7

Q7 · Map the nervous system

(a) [4]

A brain

B spinal cord

C cranial nerves

D spinal nerves.

Use the actual leader endpoints, not the positions of the letters.

(b) [2] Central: A and B. Peripheral: C and D.

The division is structural, not based on whether an action is voluntary.

(c) [2] Cranial: 12 pairs. Spinal: 31 pairs.

Do not confuse pairs with the number of individual nerves.

Review Answer · Q8

Q8 · Responding to an alarm

(a) [3] Stimulus: sound of the alarm. Receptor organ: ear. Effector: hand/finger muscles.

The alarm is the sound source; the stimulus is its sound. The hand muscles carry out the response.

(b) [3] Sensory nerves carry impulses from receptors to the brain. The brain interprets the information and coordinates a decision. Motor nerves carry impulses to the muscles.

Information flow must have the correct direction.

Q9 · Actions and control

(a) [4] i voluntary ii involuntary iii involuntary iv voluntary.

10 A rapid protective response
10 Gerak balas perlindungan yang cepat
A person accidentally touches a sharp edge. The events below are not in order:
Seseorang tersentuh tepi tajam secara tidak sengaja. Peristiwa berikut tidak mengikut urutan:
Event
M motor impulses reach arm muscles
impuls motor sampai ke otot lengan
W the muscles contract and the hand withdraws
otot mengecut dan tangan ditarik
R skin receptors detect the stimulus
reseptor kulit mengesan rangsangan
S harmful contact
sentuhan berbahaya
C sensory impulses reach the spinal cord and a response is coordinated.
impuls deria sampai ke saraf tunjang dan gerak balas diselaraskan.
Do not test this with a sharp object.
Jangan uji dengan objek tajam.
(a) Arrange the five labelled events in the correct order, starting with S. [3]
Susun lima peristiwa berlabel mengikut urutan yang betul, bermula dengan S.
(b) Why is this response useful even though the person has not first decided to move the hand? [2]

Review Answer · Q10

Q10 · A rapid protective response

(a) [3] S→R→C→M→W.

The supplied C event includes spinal processing; the quick withdrawal does not need a prior conscious decision.

(b) [2] It produces a rapid withdrawal, reducing continued contact with the harmful object and the risk of further injury.

Speed and protection are linked; do not claim that every injury is prevented.

(c) [1] No. Information can also travel to the brain for awareness, while the rapid withdrawal is coordinated through the spinal reflex pathway.

The spinal reflex pathway does not imply isolation from the brain.

Review Answer · Q10

Q10 · A rapid protective response

(a) [3] S→R→C→M→W.

The supplied C event includes spinal processing; the quick withdrawal does not need a prior conscious decision.

(b) [2] It produces a rapid withdrawal, reducing continued contact with the harmful object and the risk of further injury.

Speed and protection are linked; do not claim that every injury is prevented.

(c) [1] No. Information can also travel to the brain for awareness, while the rapid withdrawal is coordinated through the spinal reflex pathway.

The spinal reflex pathway does not imply isolation from the brain.

Review Answer · Q11

Q11 · Comparing reaction speed

(a) [2] A:(12+15+11+14+13)÷5=13 cm. B:(20+22+19+21+23)÷5=21 cm.

The same five-trial method is used for both students.

(b) [2]

A its mean distance 13 cm is shorter than B’s 21 cm.

A shorter fall before catching indicates a quicker response under the same conditions.

(c) [2]

Same ruler same initial zero alignment and hand position.

Accept / Terima: Same release method; supported catching hand; no advance warning for both

Release method, hand support and lack of advance warning are also valid controlled conditions.

(d) [2] The warning allows B to anticipate the release and prepare to catch, which may shorten the fall. The release conditions differ, so the distance difference cannot be attributed only to the students’ reaction speed.

Compare under the same release conditions. Falling distance is an indicator of response speed, not a direct time reading.

13 A disrupted pathway
13 Laluan yang terganggu
In a fictional case, a motor nerve pathway from the central nervous system to some hand muscles is damaged. The person can still describe the intended movement.

(b) The person can still feel a gentle touch on the hand although moving it is difficult. Explain how this is possible. [2]

Review Answer · Q13

Q13 · A disrupted pathway

(a) [2] Damage may interrupt motor impulses travelling to the muscles. The muscles may not contract normally to produce the intended hand movement.

The case specifies a damaged motor pathway; do not assume every brain or nerve injury has the same effect.

(b) [2] The sensory receptors and sensory pathway can still carry information about touch to the central nervous system. The damaged motor pathway affects signals to muscles, so sensory detection can remain while movement is impaired.

Sensory input and motor output have different roles; the given injury does not imply both pathways fail.

Exercise Q14 & 15

Answer the questions first. Check the answers and explanations only when ready.Jawab soalan dahulu. Semak jawapan dan penerangan apabila sudah bersedia.

Question 14

A student shifts her gaze from a distant wall clock to a nearby label. The room lighting stays the same. Which change increases the eye’s refractive power to focus the nearby label sharply on the retina?
Seorang murid mengalihkan pandangan daripada jam dinding yang jauh kepada label yang dekat. Pencahayaan bilik tidak berubah. Perubahan manakah meningkatkan kuasa pembiasan mata untuk memfokuskan imej label yang dekat dengan jelas pada retina?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: C

[1] C — The eye lens becomes thicker.

Jawapan yang betul: C — Kanta mata menjadi lebih tebal.

C: a thicker lens provides greater focusing power for a near object. A and D change the light-entry aperture, not lens accommodation; B is the opposite distance adjustment.

Question 15

A learner detects a faint shape in a dim storeroom but cannot identify its colour reliably. Which explanation best fits this observation?
Seorang murid mengesan bentuk samar dalam stor yang malap tetapi tidak dapat mengenal pasti warnanya dengan pasti. Penjelasan manakah paling sesuai?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: A

[1] A — Rod cells detect dim light but do not distinguish colours.

Jawapan yang betul: A — Sel rod mengesan cahaya malap tetapi tidak membezakan warna.

A explains both observations. C incorrectly assigns colour discrimination to rods. B incorrectly makes cones more sensitive than rods in dim light. D gives both incorrect dim-light sensitivity and incorrect absence of colour discrimination to cones.

Exercise Q16 & 17

Answer the questions first. Check the answers and explanations only when ready.Jawab soalan dahulu. Semak jawapan dan penerangan apabila sudah bersedia.

Question 16

The eardrum and ossicles vibrate normally, but sensory receptor cells in the cochlea are damaged. Which stage is most directly affected?
Gegendang telinga dan osikel bergetar secara normal, tetapi sel reseptor deria dalam koklea rosak. Peringkat manakah paling terjejas secara langsung?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: D

[1] D — Producing nerve signals when receptors are stimulated.

Jawapan yang betul: D — Menghasilkan isyarat saraf apabila reseptor dirangsang.

D is the sensory-receptor stage. A and B precede the intact eardrum; C is stated to function normally. Fluid motion alone does not produce nerve impulses without functioning sensory cells.

Question 17

During a cold, a learner can still detect that a drink is sweet, but finds its fruit flavour harder to identify. What best explains this difference?
Semasa selesema, seorang murid masih dapat mengesan bahawa minuman itu manis tetapi lebih sukar mengenal pasti perisa buahnya. Apakah penjelasan terbaik?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: B

[1] B — Fewer aroma molecules reach the smell receptors, while taste receptors can still respond.

Jawapan yang betul: B — Lebih sedikit molekul aroma sampai kepada reseptor bau, manakala reseptor rasa masih boleh bergerak balas.

B explains impaired fruit-aroma identification with preserved sweetness. A invents separate fruit-specific basic tastes; C swaps taste and smell roles. D places the main reduction at taste buds and preserves smell, the opposite of the nasal-blockage mechanism described.

Exercise Q18 & 19

Answer the questions first. Check the answers and explanations only when ready.Jawab soalan dahulu. Semak jawapan dan penerangan apabila sudah bersedia.

Question 18

Two blunt tips are gently touched to skin at the same separation. Site P is identified as two contacts more often than site Q. Which explanation is consistent with this result?
Dua hujung tumpul disentuhkan perlahan-lahan pada kulit dengan jarak pemisahan yang sama. Tapak P lebih kerap dikenal pasti sebagai dua sentuhan berbanding tapak Q. Penjelasan manakah selaras dengan keputusan ini?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: D

[1] D — P has more touch receptors per unit area than Q.

Jawapan yang betul: D — P mempunyai lebih banyak reseptor sentuhan per unit luas berbanding Q.

D is consistent with greater spatial sensitivity. A and C predict the opposite result. B is not established by the observations and would not explain the stated result using the school sensitivity model.

Question 19

In a simplified eye model, approximately parallel rays from a distant sign meet before the retina. Which corrective lens should be placed in front of the eye?
Dalam model mata ringkas, sinar hampir selari daripada papan tanda jauh bertemu sebelum retina. Kanta pembetulan manakah perlu diletakkan di hadapan mata?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: C

[1] C — A concave lens, to make incoming rays diverge before the eye focuses them.

Jawapan yang betul: C — Kanta cekung, untuk mencapahkan sinar masuk sebelum mata memfokuskannya.

C corrects the stated myopic focus. A increases an already excessive convergence; B targets astigmatism rather than the stated focus position; D does not shift the focus.

Question 20

A task requires an image of structures inside the body using reflected high-frequency sound rather than X-rays. Which device meets the requirement?
Satu tugasan memerlukan imej struktur di dalam badan menggunakan pantulan bunyi berfrekuensi tinggi dan bukannya sinar-X. Alat manakah memenuhi keperluan ini?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: A

[1] A — Ultrasound scanner

Jawapan yang betul: A — Pengimbas ultrabunyi

A uses ultrasound echoes. D and B resolve small specimens rather than the requested internal sound image. C uses the excluded X-ray radiation.

Question 21

In a one-eye demonstration, a marker disappears at a particular viewing distance while another marker remains visible. Its image falls at the optic-nerve exit. Why is it not detected?
Dalam demonstrasi menggunakan sebelah mata, satu tanda hilang pada jarak pandangan tertentu manakala tanda lain masih kelihatan. Imejnya jatuh pada tempat saraf optik keluar. Mengapakah tanda itu tidak dikesan?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: D

[1] D — There are no photoreceptors at that retinal region.

Jawapan yang betul: D — Tiada fotoreseptor pada kawasan retina itu.

D explains the absence of light detection at the optic-nerve exit. B and C still provide photoreceptors that can detect appropriate light; A describes a receptor-rich region rather than a blind spot.

Question 22

A teacher uses a pinhole card to project the Sun onto a screen. Which viewing arrangement is safe?
Seorang guru menggunakan kad berlubang jarum untuk mengunjurkan Matahari pada skrin. Susunan pemerhatian manakah selamat?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: B

[1] B — Keep the Sun behind you and look only at the projected image on the screen.

Jawapan yang betul: B — Pastikan Matahari di belakang anda dan lihat imej unjuran pada skrin sahaja.

B is indirect projection. A gives inadequate protection; C is direct viewing; D still risks retinal injury. An eclipse does not make direct viewing safe.

Question 23

Two learners compare the highest frequency they can detect using quiet tones. Which procedure makes their comparison fairer without increasing risk?
Dua orang murid membandingkan frekuensi tertinggi yang dapat dikesan menggunakan nada perlahan. Prosedur manakah menjadikan perbandingan lebih adil tanpa meningkatkan risiko?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: C

[1] C — Keep the equipment, low sound level and distance the same for both learners.

Jawapan yang betul: C — Kekalkan peralatan, aras bunyi rendah dan jarak yang sama bagi kedua-dua murid.

C controls conditions. A changes intensity and can increase exposure; B confounds equipment/distance; D selectively removes data. School 20 Hz–20 kHz is approximate, not guaranteed for every individual.

Review Answer · Q25

Q25 · Two pathways and changing light

(a) [2]

Cornea→aqueous humour→pupil→eye lens.

Eye lens→vitreous humour→retina, continuing the same correct sequence.

The optical path ends at retinal receptors. Thereafter information travels as nerve impulses.

Pupil dilation admits more light in dim conditions and is not the same process as lens accommodation.

(b) [2]

Nerve impulses, not light.

Through the optic nerve to the brain for interpretation.

(c) [2]

The pupil becomes larger.

More light enters the eye.

Rajah E2 dan E3 menunjukkan mata ringkas tanpa pembetulan. E2 menerima sinar selari daripada objek jauh; E3 menerima sinar mencapah daripada objek dekat. Garis putus-putus menunjukkan lanjutan unjuran, bukan cahaya yang diperhatikan keluar daripada mata.

Review Answer · Q26

Q26 · Different focusing errors

(a) [4]

E2: short-sightedness concave lens.

E3: long-sightedness convex lens.

The focal position determines the stated refractive defect. Concave lenses reduce net convergence for myopia; convex lenses add convergence for hyperopia. Astigmatism involves unequal curvature, not simply a focus too far forward or backward.

(b) [2]

E2: eyeball too long or focusing power too strong.

E3: eyeball too short or focusing power too weak.

Accept / Terima: School model: eye lens too thick for E2 / too thin for E3.

(c) [2]

Astigmatism.

Cylindrical lens.

Review Answer · Q27

Q27 · Appearance and evidence

(a) [2]

No both measured diameters are 12.0 mm.

Optical illusion.

Measurements distinguish actual geometry from perceived appearance. Retinal blindspot loss depends on an image falling on a receptor-free region; a vehicle blind zone concerns the available field of view and does not establish that retinal mechanism.

(b) [2]

Its image falls on the blind spot.

This optic-nerve exit region has no photoreceptors to detect light.

(c) [1] A vehicle blind zone can result from limited field of view or obstruction, unlike the retinal region without photoreceptors.

Review Answer · Q28

Q28 · Tools extend sight

(a) [5]

1 light microscope

2 scanning electron microscope

3 binoculars

4 ultrasound scanner

5 X-ray machine.

Each tool is matched to both scale and imaging mechanism. Electron and light microscopy differ; ultrasound is sound-based, not X-ray-based. Curved transparent bottle surfaces refract light but do not make solar viewing safe.

Never aim it at the Sun or use it to view the Sun.

Q30 · A vibration model

Eardrum.

Sound makes the membrane vibrate, moving the grains.

Review Answer · Q31

Q31 · Detecting an odour

(a) [2]

X nasal cavity.

Y smell/olfactory receptors.

Smell receptors occupy the upper nasal region. Dissolution in mucus precedes receptor stimulation; nerves carry impulses, not the odour chemicals themselves. Practical safety excludes unknown or irritating substances.

(b) [2]

Odour chemicals dissolve in mucus and stimulate smell receptors.

Nerves carry impulses to the brain for interpretation.

(c) [1] Use only teacher-approved non-irritating materials; avoid known allergens or direct deep inhalation.

Accept / Terima: Gently waft the aroma; never smell unknown laboratory chemicals.

Q32 · Taste and dissolved substances

(a) [5]

Accept / Terima: Any familiar safe food dominated by the stated taste, such as honey, lime, salted food, unsweetened bitter cocoa or mushrooms.

The simulated totals are 14 and 5. Nose condition affects aroma access, while basic taste can remain. Rinsing reduces carry-over; controlled amounts/temperature and allergy precautions support an interpretable, safer comparison.

(b) [2]

An open nose allows more aroma molecules to reach smell receptors.

Smell contributes to flavour identification while the tongue can still detect basic tastes.

(c) [2]

Nose condition: open or gently pinched.

Removes residual taste/aroma to reduce carry-over between samples.

(d) [1] Check food allergies and use clean individual utensils; exclude unsafe samples.

Review Answer · Q36

Q36 · Using skin information

(a) [2]

It can distinguish closely spaced raised dots.

A high density of touch receptors supports this sensitivity.

Braille relies on spatial touch discrimination. A skin temperature sensation is qualitative and condition-dependent, so it cannot substitute for a calibrated numerical thermometer.

(b) [2]

It provides a sensation of warmth/coolness.

A sensation does not give an exact numerical temperature and varies with conditions/person.

Review Answer · Q37

Q37 · Protecting and combining senses

(a) [3]

Noise: protective earmuffs or earplugs.

Arc welding: suitable filtered welding helmet/face protection.

Fire smoke: full-face self-contained breathing apparatus with air cylinder, for trained firefighters.

Protection must match the hazard: audio headphones are not hearing PPE; dark goggles alone are inadequate for arc welding; filter masks do not replace supplied breathing air in dangerous fire atmospheres. Phone reading and vibration combine light and mechanical stimuli.

(b) [2]

Sight: light from the displayed message.

Touch: mechanical vibration of the phone.

(c) [2]

Use adequate lighting/appropriate viewing distance or take regular breaks.

Keep sound volume low/reduce exposure time ordinary headphones are not protective earmuffs.

Q38 · Hearing range and helpful technology

(a) [2]

Tone B: 1 000 Hz.

Hearing varies with age/individual condition and audibility also depends on sound level.

The nominal frequency range describes a reference, not an individual diagnosis.

Stethoscopes and loudspeakers serve different listening purposes. Hearing-aid amplification differs from implant stimulation; device suitability requires specialist assessment.

(c) [2]

A hearing aid amplifies sound entering the ear.

A cochlear implant provides electrical stimulation to the auditory nerve pathway, bypassing damaged sensory cells specialist assessment is needed.

Exercise Q50 & 51

Answer the questions first. Check the answers and explanations only when ready.Jawab soalan dahulu. Semak jawapan dan penerangan apabila sudah bersedia.

Question 50

An animal has forward-facing eyes with a large overlap between their fields of vision. 50. Which advantage is most directly linked to this overlap? [1]
Seekor haiwan mempunyai mata yang menghadap ke hadapan dengan pertindihan besar antara medan penglihatannya. Kelebihan manakah paling berkaitan dengan pertindihan ini?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: B

[1] B: Judging a target’s distance more accurately

Jawapan yang betul: B — Menilai jarak sasaran dengan lebih tepat

Overlap supports binocular depth information. Colour and dim-light detection depend on other sensory properties, not overlap alone.

Question 51

A sound reaches a rabbit’s left ear slightly earlier and more loudly than its right ear. 51. Which explanation is best? [1]
Bunyi sampai ke telinga kiri arnab sedikit lebih awal dan lebih kuat berbanding telinga kanannya. Penjelasan manakah paling tepat?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: A

[1] A: The brain compares arrival time and loudness, indicating a source on the left.

Jawapan yang betul: A — Otak membandingkan masa ketibaan dan kekuatan bunyi, menunjukkan sumber di kiri.

Time and loudness differences provide direction information; the nearer ear receives the sound earlier/louder.

Question 52

For this item, use these approximate ranges: human 20–20 000 Hz; elephant 16–12 000 Hz; dog 67–45 000 Hz; bat 2 000–110 000 Hz. Treat both limits as included and assume the sound is loud enough to be detected. 52. Which listed animal could detect an 18 Hz sound according to the given data? [1]
Untuk item ini, gunakan julat anggaran berikut: manusia 20–20 000 Hz; gajah 16–12 000 Hz; anjing 67–45 000 Hz; kelawar 2 000–110 000 Hz. Anggap kedua-dua had termasuk dalam julat dan bunyi cukup kuat untuk dikesan. Haiwan yang manakah boleh mengesan bunyi 18 Hz mengikut data yang diberikan?
Correct Answer / Jawapan Betul: D

[1] D: Elephant

Jawapan yang betul: D — Gajah

18 Hz lies within 16–12 000 Hz but below each other given lower limit.

Question 53

A fish uses a lateral line to detect water disturbances. An insect releases pheromone during communication. 53. Which classification is correct? [1]
Ikan menggunakan garis lateral untuk mengesan gangguan air. Serangga membebaskan feromon semasa komunikasi. Pengelasan manakah betul?

[1] C: The lateral line is a sensory organ; releasing pheromone is a response.

Jawapan yang betul: C — Garis lateral ialah organ deria; pembebasan feromon ialah gerak balas.

A detection structure is distinguished from an action/output.

(c) [1] Valid sensory ability and matching survival use, e.g.stereophonic hearing locates approaching predators so prey can escape

Accept / Terima: Stereoscopic depth estimation aids hunting; wider visual field detects threats
